Our medical expert says

“The Sure Pro is one of the most flexible mid‑to‑high‑range stimulators in our selection: 15 programs — 12 preset and 3 manually configurable — two channels and a rechargeable battery. Its special feature is tibial nerve stimulation (TIBN): our only device with this function, offering an alternative to probe treatment for urge incontinence. If your treating physician recommended multiple approaches, this single device covers them. You may find my article Treatment of incontinence in practice useful.”

Realistic expectations
Pelvic floor muscle builds like any other muscle: with frequent sessions, measurable change typically appears after 6–12 weeks — don’t expect results from just one or two sessions. TIBN is delivered over the inner ankle with surface electrodes — no probe. Many find this more acceptable, but reaching a noticeable effect still usually requires several weeks to months of regular treatment. The first days are about learning: correct probe insertion and intensity setting take practice.
Not the right device for you if
you want objective biofeedback about your muscle work — the Sure Pro only stimulates, it does not provide biofeedback.
Before you order
Correct diagnosis is key: stress, urge and mixed incontinence need different programs, so determining the type is a medical task. The product description gives general guidance on program selection and treatment time; your treating physician or pelvic‑floor therapist can advise what suits you best. DO NOT use during pregnancy or when trying to conceive, with a pacemaker or implanted defibrillator, with active urinary or vaginal infection, within six weeks after childbirth or pelvic surgery, with severe urinary retention, or when pelvic‑region sensation is reduced; in epilepsy use only after medical consultation. The probe is for single‑user hygiene — it must not be shared and should be replaced over time.

– Dr. Zátrok Zsolt
Physician, medical technology expert, blogger

Who is it recommended for?

The STRE 1 and STRE 2 programs stimulate fast muscle fibres with targeted frequencies — they may help increase urethral closure pressure. The two stress programs operate at different frequencies, so choose per your physician’s recommendation.

Besides the URGE 1–2 programs, the Sure Pro offers a unique option: the TIBN programs use ankle electrodes to non‑invasively target bladder overactivity. If probe treatment is uncomfortable or you want a complementary therapy, TIBN is an alternative.

The MIXED program is designed for combined treatment of stress and urge incontinence — it targets both issues in one session. The two‑channel design lets you use probe stimulation and TIBN simultaneously.

The PAIN program uses TENS technology to target chronic pelvic pain. It can be used as needed, even daily.

The SENS program is specifically designed for neural stimulation after sensory loss — when pelvic floor muscle sensation is reduced (e.g. after surgery or nerve damage). This program is not available on many other devices.

How does electrostimulation work?

The Sure Pro offers multiple therapeutic approaches in a single device:

Pelvic floor stimulation (with probe): Gentle electrical pulses delivered via the vaginal probe cause the pelvic floor muscles to contract and relax. This cyclic training can help restore muscle strength and improve bladder control.

Tibial nerve stimulation (TIBN — with ankle electrodes): Stimulating the tibial nerve at the ankle aims to reduce bladder hyperactivity. Percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation (PTNS) is an accepted clinical treatment for urge incontinence — the Sure Pro offers its transcutaneous (surface) variant for home use.

TENS pain relief: The PAIN program targets chronic pelvic pain using the gate‑control theory.

The Sure Pro does not include a biofeedback function. If you need objective feedback on training effectiveness, consider the evoStim P (pressure‑biofeedback) or the evoStim E (EMG‑biofeedback) devices.

Frequently asked questions

The tibial nerve runs along the inner side of the ankle and is connected to the pelvic‑floor nervous system. Stimulation via surface electrodes aims to reduce bladder hyperactivity — non‑invasively and without a probe. It is the home, transcutaneous variant of PTNS used in clinical settings.

No. Electrostimulation devices are contraindicated during pregnancy. Start treatment only after postnatal medical clearance (typically 6–8 weeks).

The Perfect PFE is single‑channel with 4 programs — simpler and more budget‑friendly. The Sure Pro is two‑channel with 15 programs, tibial nerve stimulation (TIBN), a rechargeable battery and a 99‑step intensity control. If you need multiple treatment approaches (probe + TIBN), the Sure Pro is the more flexible choice.

The Sure Pro does not include biofeedback — the device does not measure muscle activity. If you need objective feedback on training progress, consider the evoStim P (pressure‑biofeedback) or the evoStim E (EMG‑biofeedback). The advantage of the Sure Pro is its wider program selection and the TIBN function.

The 3 manual programs let you save individual parameters (frequency, pulse width, treatment time) as recommended by your clinician. This is especially useful when preset programs don't precisely meet therapeutic needs.

With regular daily use of 20–30 minutes, improvement is usually noticeable within 4–12 weeks. The effectiveness of TIBN programs has been evaluated in systematic studies over 12‑week treatment periods. The treatment memory helps track regularity.

How to use the Sure Pro?

1

Select the program

Use the backlit LCD to select one of the 15 programs. Incontinence: STRE, URGE, MIXED. Pelvic floor training: PFW A/B, ENDUR. Pain: PAIN. Tibial nerve: TIBN 1–2. Sensory loss: SENS. The 3 manual programs allow custom settings.

2

Connect the probe or electrodes

For probe treatment: moisten the supplied vaginal probe with the included Go Gel contact gel. For TIBN treatment: place the adhesive electrodes on the inner side of the ankle. You can work on both channels at once — probe + ankle electrode combination.

3

Set the intensity

Choose a comfortable but effective intensity per channel from 99 levels (1 mA steps). Treatment should never be painful. The device remembers the last setting and automatically restores it at the next power‑up.

4

Perform the treatment

The program controls the pulses automatically. You can track the remaining time on the LCD. The treatment memory logs daily use so you can monitor consistency.

5

Regular use

Once daily, 20–30 minutes. TIBN is typically applied 1–2 times per week. Improvements are usually noticeable with regular treatment within 4–12 weeks. The treatment memory helps track regular use.

Package contents

The Sure Pro comes with the following accessories:

  • 1 pc TensCare Sure Pro device (built‑in rechargeable battery)
  • 1 pc vaginal probe
  • 2 pcs stimulation cables
  • 4 pcs adhesive electrodes (50×50 mm) — for TIBN treatment
  • 1 pc mains adapter (charger)

Probes are for personal use for hygiene reasons. Replacement probes, spare electrodes and contact gel can be purchased from the incontinence category.

When NOT to use the device?

Important information

The TensCare Sure Pro is CE‑marked, a Class II medical device (manufactured according to MDR, ISO 13485), designed to complement medical treatment. A medical evaluation is required before starting treatment to determine the type of incontinence.

Evidence from clinical studies supports the effectiveness of pelvic floor muscle training supplemented with electrostimulation. The effectiveness of tibial nerve stimulation (PTNS/TTNS) for overactive bladder is also supported by systematic reviews.1,2

The information on this page is for guidance only. Home therapeutic devices are intended to complement medical treatment and do not replace it. Consult your treating physician in case of symptoms.

The product description contains general advice on program selection and treatment time; your treating physician or pelvic floor therapist can advise what is ideal for you. DO NOT use during pregnancy or when attempting pregnancy, if you have a pacemaker or implanted defibrillator, with an active urinary or vaginal infection, within six weeks after childbirth or pelvic surgery, in severe urinary retention, or when pelvic sensation is reduced; in epilepsy use only after medical consultation. The probe is for personal use only—for hygiene reasons it must not be shared and should be replaced over time.

– Dr. Zsolt Zátrok
Physician, medical technology expert, blogger

Who is it for?

Urine leakage occurs during physical exertion because of weak sphincter muscles. The Perfect PFE Stress program trains fast muscle fibres at 35–40 Hz for 20 minutes daily. Clinical trials have shown a reduction in the frequency of stress incontinence episodes.

Bladder overactivity causes a sudden, uncontrollable urge to urinate. The Urge program uses a low frequency (10–12 Hz) to calm bladder muscle overactivity. Daily 20‑minute use regularly can lead to noticeable improvement.

If stress and urge symptoms occur together, treatment can be split into two parts: the first 10 minutes on the Stress program (fast fibres), the second 10 minutes on the Urge program (bladder calming). The Perfect PFE includes both programs.

The Tone maintenance program can also be used to preserve muscle strength. If uterine or bladder prolapse is present, read my detailed article on treatment of uterine prolapse.

The Pain program uses TENS technology to target chronic pelvic pain. In cases of pain it may be used regularly, even daily, for up to 40 minutes.

Treatment in practice – detailed guide →

How does electrostimulation work?

The Perfect PFE delivers gentle electrical impulses to the pelvic floor muscles via the vaginal probe. The impulses cause the muscles to contract and relax – this cyclical training can help restore muscle strength and improve bladder control.

The stress programs target fast (phasic) muscle fibres with higher frequencies, which can contribute to increased urethral closure pressure. The urge program uses a lower frequency aimed at reducing bladder muscle hyperactivity. The pain relief program operates on TENS principles – it may help reduce the perception of pain.

The Perfect PFE does not include a biofeedback function – the device does not measure muscle activity. If you need objective feedback on training effectiveness, consider the evoStim P (pressure biofeedback) or the evoStim E (EMG biofeedback) devices.

How to use the Perfect PFE

1

Select the program

Use the control button to select one of the 4 programs: Stress (stress incontinence), Urge (urge), Tone (maintenance) or Pain (pain relief). For mixed incontinence, run the Stress and Urge programs one after the other.

2

Insert the probe

Moisten the supplied vaginal probe with water or contact gel and insert it comfortably. Connect the cable to the device.

3

Set the intensity

Gradually increase the intensity until you feel a definite but comfortable muscle contraction. The treatment should not be painful – if it is, reduce the intensity.

4

Complete the treatment

The program controls the pulses automatically – you only need to get comfortable. The Stress and Urge programs last 20 minutes, the Pain program 40 minutes. The device switches off automatically at the end of the session.

5

Regular use

Use once daily for 20 minutes. Improvements are typically felt with regular treatment within 4–12 weeks. Once muscle strength is achieved, switch to the Tone program (twice weekly) for maintenance.

Important information

The Perfect PFE is a CE‑marked medical device (MDR) intended as an adjunct to medical treatment. A medical assessment is required before starting treatment to determine the type of incontinence.

Electrostimulation can be an effective adjunct to pelvic floor muscle training. The Cochrane review's 2022 comprehensive analysis found high‑level evidence for the effectiveness of pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) in treating incontinence.1

The information on this page is for guidance only. Home therapeutic devices are intended to complement medical treatment, not to replace it. Consult your treating physician in case of symptoms.

Scientific background

Clinical evidence supports the effectiveness of pelvic floor muscle training augmented with electrostimulation:

HELPI:
Our medical expert says

“Penis rings — or constriction rings — work on a simple mechanical principle: by gently compressing the base of the penis they reduce venous outflow, which helps maintain an erection. This can be especially useful for men who achieve an erection but it does not last long (so‑called venous leak), or for those bothered by premature ejaculation. The Helpi Ring is CE‑certified and drug‑free — however, the underlying cause of erectile dysfunction should always be investigated.”

Realistic expectations
The ring helps maintain an existing erection; it does not create one. Its effect on premature ejaculation varies between individuals: some notice a benefit, others do not. Safety rule: a constriction ring should be worn for a maximum of 30 minutes at a time.
This is not the right device for you if
no erection occurs at all — vacuum systems are designed for that: the Medintim Manual with manual pump, or the Medintim Active with motorised pump. If you just want the simplest entry‑level option for trying a ring, the Backup Ring silicone ring may be sufficient.
Before you order
For persistent or severe symptoms I recommend a full urological evaluation: treatable medical conditions can underlie erectile problems. In case of anticoagulant treatment or bleeding disorders, or if you are prone to prolonged, painful erections (priapism), use only after medical consultation. If you experience pain, numbness or discoloration, remove the ring immediately.

– Dr. Zsolt Zátrok
Physician, medical technology expert, blogger

Who might this be suitable for?

Premature ejaculation is one of the most common male intimate problems. The mechanical effect of the Helpi® Ring can contribute to better control and a calmer sexual experience — without medication.

Some men achieve an erection but it subsides too soon — often due to premature venous outflow (venous leak). A ring can help maintain the erection in these cases.

If you prefer not to use tablets, creams or gels, a mechanical penis ring is a simple alternative. Used with a vacuum pump it can also assist in achieving an erection — see the Manual and Active Erection System devices.

How does it work? – Mechanism of action

An erection is maintained when blood remains in the corpora cavernosa of the penis. In some men blood drains back too early (venous leak), causing the erection to subside prematurely. A constriction ring placed at the base of the penis applies gentle pressure that reduces this outflow, helping the erection last longer — without drugs or active ingredients, by a mechanical effect.

The same mild constriction can also contribute to delaying ejaculation. The Helpi® Ring is applied to an erect penis using the included applicator sleeve and can be removed easily at the end of use.

Frequently asked questions

It is recommended to wear a constriction ring for no more than 30 minutes at a time. Do not exceed this. If you experience any pain, numbness or discoloration, remove the ring immediately.

Use with anticoagulant therapy or bleeding disorders requires special caution. In such cases consult your treating physician before use.

Yes, the ring helps maintain an erection after orgasm, allowing intercourse to continue. Once the ring is removed the erection typically subsides within seconds.

The Helpi® Ring can be used on its own to maintain an erection. If you need help achieving an erection, vacuum devices are the appropriate solution — those devices come with their own constriction rings. See our penis erection aids.

How to use it? Step by step

1

Place the ring on the applicator sleeve

Stretch the ring over the included blue applicator sleeve.

2

Apply to the penis

Place the sleeve with the ring onto the erect penis and push it down toward the base.

3

Position the ring

Slide the ring off the sleeve onto the penis, then remove the sleeve. From this point the Helpi® Ring helps maintain the erection — including after orgasm.

G6726:
The G-Trode hand-held electrode can be used with the G-Pulse beauty-care programmes of Globus electrostimulator devices.

People who visit a beauty therapist are probably familiar with various electrical treatments intended to improve facial skin elasticity and reduce wrinkles and crow's feet. You cannot expect much from a single treatment, while visiting a beauty therapist every day is not an option for most people. These beauty-care programmes are already available in devices made by Globus. This means that treatments carried out at home, for a few minutes each day, can provide genuinely visible results. For this, you need a device that includes the G-Pulse programme package.

About the G-Pulse programmes

The G-Pulse programmes are microcurrent treatments created by cosmetologists and optimised for beauty care. They can primarily be used to treat wrinkles, stretch marks and skin imperfections.

After the age of thirty, the skin's metabolism begins to slow down, gradually changing the skin tissues. The renewal process becomes increasingly weaker. As a result, the skin becomes thinner and loses elasticity.

The collagen level in the skin decreases, while fibrotic elements increase. As a consequence, the skin loses its firmness and radiance and becomes dry and brittle. Wrinkles and chromatic (colour) changes appear and gradually become more numerous.

Main benefits of microcurrent treatment

  • safe and comfortable treatment - the electrical impulses are so mild that they cannot be felt and therefore cause no discomfort
  • excellent for reducing both acute and chronic pain
  • accelerates regeneration in inflammation, wear-related and degenerative conditions
  • accelerates the healing of injuries, wounds and bone fractures
  • stimulates collagen fibre production, improves skin elasticity and stimulates the healing of scars and ulcers (which is why it is widely used in beauty care!).
  • there is no habituation.
  • there are no side effects.

G-Pulse treatments

A special G-Trode treatment head is needed to carry out G-Pulse treatments. It is included as standard with the Activa 700 device; it must be purchased separately for other devices (Runner Pro, Cycling Pro, Triathlon Pro, Moto Pro, Soccer Pro).

The treatment should be carried out directly on wrinkles and the skin imperfections to be treated. As this is an electrical treatment, contact gel must be used to transmit the impulses. Apply a pea-sized amount to the skin. Place both balls of the G-Trode treatment head on the skin (both must remain in continuous contact with the skin). Move it outwards from the centre line, making small circular movements.

The device indicates when the programme has stopped.

You may enhance the effect of the treatment with cosmetics. First apply the cosmetic to the skin, rub it in and allow it to absorb. Then apply the contact gel and carry out the treatment with it. Cosmetics do not replace the gel!

When will the results be visible?

Wrinkles and other skin imperfections begin to decrease after the first treatment, then gradually disappear. New collagen filling the grooves makes the skin look fresher and smoother.

Microcurrent G-Pulse treatment increases energy production in the skin cells of the treated area, which initiates collagen production in the mitochondria. Regular use is recommended for the effect to develop. As remodelling of the skin tissues takes time, visible changes can be expected after 40-50 treatments. However, this effect is lasting and can be maintained with further treatments.

The regenerative mechanism of G-Pulse consists of two phases:

  1. The microcurrent stimulation of G-Pulse provides the energy (ATP) needed for cell metabolism and protein synthesis. As numerous studies have shown, microstimulation regenerates cells and restores tissue vitality.
  2. As it passes through the tissues, microstimulation increases microcirculation and the temperature of the treated area. As a result, nutrient uptake improves, and fibroblast cells are forced to produce the collagen needed to restore the skin's tone and elasticity.

Uses of G-Pulse

You can find numerous programmes in the device for improving the skin. Please note! The range and programme package may differ between devices, so check the details before buying!

  • Breast microlifting (Microlifting of the breasts. For example, after pregnancy.)
  • Wrinkles
  • Expression wrinkles
  • Nail strengthening
  • Hematoma
  • Face microlifting
  • Cellulite
  • Bio Skin Collagen
  • Eyes wrinkles
  • Stretch marks (fading of red discolouration)
  • Bio Peeling
  • Cleavage microlifting
  • Skin elasticity

Which devices include this programme?

Many devices made by Globus provide G-Pulse treatments

  • Runner Pro, Cycling Pro, Triathlon Pro, Moto Pro, Soccer Pro (the price of these does not include the G-Trode treatment head, which must be purchased separately)
  • Activa 700 (the price of the device also includes the G-Trode treatment head)

Recommendations for using the G-Trode treatment head

  • Select the appropriate electrostimulation programme on the device, then move the hand-held electrode over the treated area using slow, circular movements.
  • Use a neutral conductive gel to increase the stimulating effect of the treatment head.
  • The effect can be enhanced by using a gel with a collagen-stimulating effect.
  • The treatment head must remain in continuous contact with your skin during treatment.
  • Keep a distance of at least 3 cm between the electrode and the eyeball!
  • Pay attention to the intensity setting when treating the facial muscles, as they are particularly sensitive.
  • Increase the intensity gradually, starting from an extremely low stimulation level and gradually raising it until the appropriate stimulation level is reached, as indicated by suitable muscle activity.
  • Use an intensity that does not cause an unpleasant sensation.
  • When treating the face, more pain = greater effect is NOT TRUE; use the appropriate intensity!

CONSISTENCY AND PATIENCE ARE NEEDED TO ACHIEVE REAL RESULTS

Changes in the skin develop over months and years. It is unrealistic to expect a change from a single treatment!

As results can only occur when the skin's collagen production reaches a certain level, only persistent treatment can produce results. It is worth assessing the effect after 40-50 treatments.

UT1032-g:
Our medical expert says

“Therapeutic ultrasound has been a fundamental tool in physiotherapy for decades. SonicRelief enables patients to continue their treatments at home – there is no need to interrupt therapy started in hospital or clinic. The 1 MHz frequency penetrates deeper tissues, and the preset, safe parameters mean you do not have to worry about dosing. I recommend it for people living with chronic joint complaints who want to reduce clinic visits. In my therapeutic ultrasound guide I describe the method in detail.”

Realistic expectations
A course-based approach: regular, repeated treatments produce results – do not expect change from a single session. It does not reverse existing joint wear; it is an adjunct treatment for pain and soft-tissue complaints. Treatment is painless and may produce only a mild warming sensation. Ultrasound gel is essential: the gel is not a comfort item but a requirement for ultrasound wave transmission.
This is not the right device for you if
you need multiple frequencies or program choices. Choose the MediSound 3000, which works at 1 and 3 MHz and offers 18 therapeutic plus 31 cosmetic programmes for clinic use. If your goal is skin care rather than musculoskeletal complaints, the IPS facial device is more appropriate and considerably cheaper.
Before you order
The product description and the dosing guide contain general advice on treatment time and frequency. Your ideal settings should be determined by the physician or physiotherapist who knows your condition. DO NOT use near a pacemaker, on the limb affected by active deep vein thrombosis, over a malignant tumour, over the abdomen or pelvis during pregnancy, on open wounds or active infections, or over areas of severe osteoporosis. Gel and replacement heads can be chosen from ultrasound accessories.

– Dr. Zsolt Zátrok
Physician, medical technology expert, blogger

What to use it for?

Does your knee hurt on the stairs, or does your shoulder or hip ache? The doctor diagnosed joint wear (osteoarthritis) or joint inflammation (arthritis). In the mornings it can take minutes for your joints to “wake up,” and some days even your usual walk feels burdensome.

1 MHz therapeutic ultrasound penetrates deeply, so it can reach larger joints – knee, shoulder, hip – and deeper muscles. Systematic reviews suggest therapeutic ultrasound can positively influence joint pain, especially in the knee. With SonicRelief you can perform the treatment at home when it suits you.

By the afternoon your neck locks up and you can only turn by rotating your whole torso? Long sitting, slouching at a screen or a bad sleeping position tightens the neck muscles – and the pain often radiates into the head and shoulder.

Did a sudden movement “throw out” your back? Does sharp pain restrict movement? Do you have a herniated disc with frequent back pain or pain radiating into the buttock or thigh?

Therapeutic ultrasound can reduce pain intensity in spine-related complaints. Treatments take only 5–10 minutes – with SonicRelief you can even perform them daily without visiting a clinic.

Is your back tight with palpable, painful knots (trigger points) around the shoulder? After training or physical work your overworked muscles ache for days, or recurring muscle cramps trouble you? Doctors call this myofascial pain.

The deep-heating effect of ultrasound can help relax tight muscles and loosen knotted, cramping areas. With SonicRelief you can target the painful spot directly – using slow, circular motions right over the affected area.

Does lifting a cup send a jolt through your elbow (tennis elbow)? Does your Achilles throb after running, or do you feel a pulling pain under the kneecap when squatting? Tendinitis and degenerative tendon changes (tendinopathy) can be insidious: without treatment they may persist for months and recur with every load.

Physiotherapists have used therapeutic ultrasound for decades to treat tendon problems. Ultrasound's microvibrations and deep-heating effect may support tendon regeneration and pain relief. SonicRelief is compact – it even fits into your gym bag.

After surgery, a cast or injury does your joint no longer bend as before? Scar tissue has hardened, tissues have adhered, range of motion is reduced – and progress in physiotherapy is slow because stretching stiff tissues is painful?

Ultrasound's deep-heating effect can soften scar tissue and help release adhesions that limit movement – warmed connective tissue becomes more pliable, making stretching exercises more effective. Apply treatment directly before physiotherapy! Ultrasound can also be used to reduce post-injury swelling (edema) – consult your treating physician beforehand in such cases.

Are the first steps in the morning the worst, as if you stepped on a nail, with stabbing pain in the heel? It eases as you move but returns after prolonged standing or walking. These are typical signs of plantar fasciitis, often associated with a heel spur visible on X-ray.

Therapeutic ultrasound has long been used in physiotherapy to treat heel pain. Ultrasound's deep-heating effect can help loosen the thickened, inflamed plantar fascia, while microvibrations may support tissue regeneration and pain relief. With SonicRelief you can target your heel at home – it's advisable to combine treatment with plantar fascia stretching exercises.

Frequently asked questions

The device may be used on the same area once daily for a maximum of 15 minutes per session. The device automatically stops after the set time. Multiple adjacent areas can be treated consecutively. For longer-lasting results it is recommended to use it regularly for 2, up to 4 weeks.

At locations distant from the chest — for example at the ankle, knee, or lumbar spine — this risk does not apply and your physician may permit use on those distant sites.

Most users feel mild warmth or slight tingling. The device does not vibrate and is not a massager – therapeutic ultrasound works at a microscopic level in the tissues. If you feel a burning sensation, it may mean you are holding the device in one spot too long or the intensity is too high. Stop the treatment or move the device faster or reduce the intensity.

Air does not conduct ultrasound — without gel the device cannot deliver energy into the tissues. Ultrasound gel ensures uninterrupted energy transfer, and without it the treatment is ineffective or will not start due to lack of contact. Always use gel specifically made for ultrasound treatments!

SonicRelief uses the same 1 MHz therapeutic ultrasound technology as physiotherapy clinics. The difference is in the safe, preset parameters: the home-use device prevents excessively high intensity and automatically stops after a maximum of 15 minutes.

Individual responses vary. Some users notice changes after only a few treatments, but for more durable results regular use for about 10–15 days is usually needed. If there is no noticeable improvement after 20–25 treatments, ultrasound is probably not the appropriate method for that complaint.

Watch it in action

In his 17-part video series, Dr. Zátrok Zsolt demonstrates step-by-step how to use therapeutic ultrasound, the correct settings and safe application.

How to use it? It's that simple:

1

Apply ultrasound gel

Clean the area of skin to be treated, then apply a generous amount of ultrasound gel.
The gel is essential for energy transmission — without it the device may not turn on and the treatment effect may be lacking!

2

Turn on the device

Press the power (ON) button.
SonicRelief operates with safe, preset parameters — no complicated settings required.

3

Set the treatment time

Use the Time button to select the treatment duration.
5, 10 and 15 minutes are available — choose 5 minutes for areas smaller than your palm, 10 minutes for palm-sized areas and 15 minutes for larger areas.

4

Set the treatment intensity

Use the Mode (treatment intensity) button to set the ultrasound intensity.
Choose L (low), M (medium) or H (high). For very recent injuries select low intensity. For persistent, multi-week or chronic complaints you may choose H (high) intensity.

5

Keep it moving

Place the device head on the skin and move it slowly in circular motions over the treatment area.
Never hold it in one spot! You may feel a mild warming sensation during treatment.
Attention! The device has a contact sensor! If there isn't enough gel or the device-skin contact is poor, ultrasound emission will stop and the LEDs will blink green.

6

Done in minutes

The device automatically stops after the set time. Turn the main switch to OFF.
Wipe remaining gel off the device and your skin. Rest the treated area. One treatment per day is recommended.

G1404:
Our medical expert says

“The Lipozero G39 is Globus's ultrasonic cavitation flagship: five frequencies – 3 MHz, 1 MHz, 526 kHz, 150 kHz and the deep-penetrating 39 kHz –, two probes and 49 programs. The 39 kHz probe is what enables targeted treatment of thicker fat layers, while the higher frequencies are for superficial skin treatments. This model is aimed more at salon practice than casual home use.”

Realistic expectations
Cosmetic device: supports skincare and body-shaping routines; it is not a treatment for disease. Cavitation is a body-contouring procedure, NOT a weight-loss method – body weight is determined by diet and exercise. The five frequencies do not make the device stronger; they let you adapt the treatment to the depth of the target tissue. Changes become appreciable after a few weeks of regular treatment and adequate fluid intake. It works alongside a comprehensive routine – nutrition, exercise, fluid intake, sleep, sun protection – not instead of it.
This device isn't for you if
You are looking for occasional, home-use skin care: for that purpose the Lipozero Excel or the G150 is usually sufficient given the required knowledge and price. The device pays off if you use it regularly, at different depths and on multiple body areas.
Before you order
The product description contains general guidance on frequency choice, treatment time and frequency. In case of uncertainty, or if you have a chronic condition or take medication, consult your treating physician before you start using the device. NOT to be used during pregnancy or if pregnancy is suspected (particularly on the abdomen and hips), over areas with thrombophlebitis, in acute infection or sepsis, in active cancer or when treating a tumor directly, and in the presence of a pacemaker or other implanted electronic device.

– Dr. Zátrok Zsolt
Physician, medical technology expert, blogger

What to use it for?

The Ultracav programs for the 39 kHz probe are designed for thicker fat layers: full-body and thigh–buttock zones, according to fat thickness (3–6 cm and over 6 cm). This is the deepest-penetrating cavitation mode in the Lipozero range.

The 150 kHz Cavimax and the multi-frequency MF-Plus programs target the appearance of cellulite (including edematous and fibrous types) and local fat deposits, covering the abdomen, hips and thighs.

The 526 kHz NorAd mode aims to support fat metabolism by stimulating noradrenaline production – particularly effective for male abdominal fat. Dedicated male programs: abdomen, hips, upper and lower limbs.

The Beauty Care program package supports firming, body shaping (abdomen, legs), drainage (arms, legs), and stretch mark treatment. The ultrasound's thermal effect and micromassage can positively influence connective tissue condition.

The superficial 3 MHz skin programs offer facial firming, wrinkle treatment, scar treatment, rosacea and photoaging programs, as well as skin restructuring and smoothing.

Mechanism of fat reduction – what happens under the skin?

When adipose tissue is treated with low-frequency ultrasound, cyclical waves generate tiny gas bubbles around fat cells (cavitation). The collapse of these bubbles exerts a micromechanical effect that can disrupt fat cell membranes and release fat droplets. The released fat is transported by the lymphatic and blood circulation, so light activity or lymphatic massage after treatment is recommended.

Meaningful cavitation effects occur almost exclusively at frequencies below 600 kHz: the lower the frequency, the deeper it penetrates tissue. For this reason the G39 includes a dedicated 39 kHz probe for thicker fat layers, 150 kHz for cellulite and moderate fat layers, 526 kHz for noradrenaline-based fat mobilization, and 3 MHz for superficial beauty treatments. Frequency modulation (MF-Plus) has been shown in studies to provide better results than a single constant frequency because it reaches tissues at different depths.

Frequently asked questions

Using cavitation ultrasound on the abdomen and hip areas is prohibited during pregnancy, and it should be avoided if pregnancy is suspected. If uncertain, consult your physician.

Treatment is contraindicated with a pacemaker or other implanted electronic device. Avoid near metal prostheses or osteosynthesis. For any implanted device, consult your doctor first.

Use the Ø 50 mm 39 kHz probe for deep cavitation of thicker fat layers (Ultracav programs), and the Ø 42 mm multi-frequency probe for cellulite, body-shaping, beauty and skin programs. Both require contact gel.

For a given body area, 2–3 treatments per week are recommended, 10–20 minutes per session, with at least 48 hours between treatments. After a course (6–8 weeks) consider a 2–3 week break.

Results vary by individual. Most users report visible improvements after a few weeks of regular use. Important: ultrasound is an adjunctive treatment – lasting results are achieved when combined with a healthy lifestyle, proper nutrition and exercise.

The Lipozero G150 is multi-frequency (3 MHz – 150 kHz) with one probe. The G39 adds an extra Ø 50 mm, 39 kHz deep-cavitation probe and the Ultracav programs for thicker fat layers – a total of 49 programs. The G39 is the professional flagship.

How to use? It's this simple:

1

Select and prepare the probe

Choose the appropriate probe: the Ø 42 mm multi-frequency probe for versatile treatments, the Ø 50 mm 39 kHz probe for deep cavitation. Clean the skin and apply ample contact gel.

2

Select the program

Turn on the device and select the program that matches your goal: Ultracav or Cavimax for fat layers, NorAd for fat mobilization, Beauty Care/Skin for superficial treatments.

3

Treatment

Start the program and move the probe continuously in circular or longitudinal motions – never leave it stationary. Adjust intensity with the Up/Down buttons to a comfortable level.

4

Finish and aftercare

At the end of the program remove residual gel. Light activity (walking, swimming) or lymphatic massage after cavitation supports the process. Wipe the probes with a damp cloth.

Physician, medical technology expert, blogger

Who and what is UniGlo good for?

The Uniwand microcurrent treatment head is specifically designed for the face: the eye area (brow lines, under-eye zone), around the mouth (marionette lines), and the forehead (frown lines). Its small size allows targeted application. The gentle microcurrent is not painful on facial skin; most users feel only a slight tingling.

EMS (electrical muscle stimulation) on the abdominal area can help develop muscle tone — it is not a substitute for conventional abdominal exercise but a COMPLEMENT. Combined with classic core exercises (plank, crunches, leg raises) you can get better results. The UniGlo 5×5 cm pads are ideal for this. Detailed explanation is in the Body shaping with muscle stimulation article.

Large muscle groups (thighs, buttocks, arms, calves) are typical EMS target areas. These can be treated with the UniGlo 5×5 cm pads. Regular EMS sessions can contribute to a firmer appearance by improving muscle tone. IMPORTANT: this DOES NOT replace active training — it is a COMPLEMENT. UniGlo is an aid within a comprehensive body-shaping routine.

Between 35 and 50 the skin’s collagen level naturally declines and fine lines appear. UniGlo’s microcurrent facial routine can be a home-based complement to a classic anti-age routine (appropriate sun protection, moisturisers, collagen serums, good sleep, balanced diet). Changes develop cumulatively over several months — do not expect instant results.

After pregnancy, following a 6–12 week pause (and with your gynaecologist’s approval), UniGlo may be applied to the abdominal/core area to gradually restore muscle tone. IMPORTANT: DO NOT use on the abdomen DURING pregnancy. It is forbidden in the first 3 months and also during the last 3–4 months of pregnancy. During breastfeeding do NOT use on the chest area.

Many people prefer home beauty routines — time saving, convenience, control. UniGlo is a device intended for independent home use and fits into evening or morning routines (even while watching TV, before or after makeup). The Uniwand is simple to use and requires no special training. Basics can be learned in 1–2 sessions following the user manual.

UniGlo performs best as part of a comprehensive routine:

  • Skincare: regular cleansing, moisturising, retinol serums, sun protection (SPF 30+).
  • Lifestyle: good sleep (7–8 hours), balanced diet (antioxidant-rich), adequate hydration.
  • Physical activity: regular exercise for an overall firmer appearance.
  • UniGlo treatment: Uniwand for facial areas, adhesive pads for larger muscle groups.

A combined approach can produce lasting effects — UniGlo is not the only tool.

IMPORTANT realistic expectations:

  • UniGlo is NOT a miracle device — results require cumulative, multi-month use.
  • It DOES NOT replace professional cosmetic or dermatological procedures (laser, mesotherapy, deep peels).
  • It DOES NOT stop age-related changes — it only supports a firmer appearance.
  • Individual response varies by skin type, age and baseline hydration.
  • Manufacturer recommends 5 sessions per week for 8–12 weeks for initial course use.
  • Long-term maintenance use is required for sustained aesthetic benefit.

Individual response depends on skin type, age and baseline condition.

How do UniGlo’s two technologies work?

UniGlo combines two electrotherapy technologies: EMS (muscle stimulation) for larger body areas and Microcurrent (MCR) for delicate facial zones.

EMS (Electrical Muscle Stimulation) induces muscle contraction by direct electrical stimulation of the muscle — the same mechanism used in classic EMS training devices. Regular EMS sessions:

  • Aim to improve muscle tone (passive “exercise-like” stimulation).
  • May support local blood circulation in the treated area.
  • As part of a comprehensive body-shaping routine can contribute to a firmer appearance.

IMPORTANT: EMS DOES NOT replace active exercise — it is a COMPLEMENT. Detailed explanation is in the EMS article.

Microcurrent (MCR/MENS) operates at VERY LOW current levels (microampere range) — users often barely feel it. This gentle technology suits facial areas:

  • It can affect the cells’ electrical environment.
  • It may support microcirculation.
  • In clinical practice it is used as part of skin rehabilitation and anti-age routines.

Microcurrent devices are traditionally part of cosmetic skincare and physiotherapy toolkits. Detailed information is in the Microcurrent article.

Classic adhesive pads cannot precisely treat the face’s delicate areas — contours, the eye zone and the lip area are too small and sensitive. The Uniwand solves this:

  • Ergonomic wand shape, easy to hold.
  • Contact-based treatment (not adhesive) — it works only where you glide it.
  • Precise targeting along contours.
  • No risk of adhesive allergy on the face.

Uniwand is compatible only with the UniGlo device — do not use it with other devices.

UniGlo pairs well with a classic anti-age skincare routine:

  • Before microcurrent: apply contact gel or a hydrating serum for conductivity.
  • After microcurrent: moisturiser, retinol serum, anti-age mask.
  • Morning routine: cleanse → microcurrent → serum → moisturiser → sun protection (SPF 30+).
  • Evening routine: remove makeup → cleanse → microcurrent → serum → night cream.

Do not alter specific therapies prescribed by your dermatologist or cosmetician because of UniGlo use.

Expected (with regular, long-term use):

  • Firmer appearance in delicate facial areas.
  • Improved muscle tone in EMS-treated body areas (when combined with active exercise).
  • Contribution as one element of a comprehensive anti-age routine.

Not expected:

  • Results equivalent to professional dermatological procedures (botox, fillers, laser, mesotherapy).
  • Complete reversal of age-related skin changes.
  • Immediate, dramatic change — results develop cumulatively over months.
  • Lasting body-shaping results without diet, exercise and sleep.

Realistic expectation = satisfied user. Miracle-expectation = disappointment.

How to use it step by step

1

Charge the battery (via USB cable)

Fully charge before first use. The rechargeable battery can be charged from any standard USB charger. A full charge allows multiple sessions.

2

Prepare the skin (body or face)

Body (EMS): clean the skin — no creams, oils or sweat. Wipe with a skin disinfectant wipe if needed.

Face (Microcurrent, Uniwand): thoroughly remove makeup and cosmetics. Before using the Uniwand apply a thin layer of contact gel or hydrating serum for good conductivity.

3

Choose the correct electrode or treatment head

The package contains three types of electrodes:

  • 4 pcs 5×5 cm: large body areas (abdomen, thighs, buttocks).
  • 4 pcs 3×5 cm: larger facial areas, arms, calves.
  • 10 pcs 25 mm round: smaller, targeted areas (e.g. around the lips).
  • 1 pc Uniwand treatment head: for delicate facial zones (around the eyes, forehead, marionette lines).
4

Select a programme (8 presets)

Choose the programme that fits your goal from UniGlo’s 8 presets — see the user manual for details. The “Microcurrent deep facial firming” programme is optimised for facial areas. The memory function stores the last used programme for quick restart.

5

Adjust intensity gradually

Start at a very low intensity. On EMS areas you should feel muscle contraction, but it must NOT be painful. For microcurrent facial treatment a barely perceptible tingling is ideal (microcurrent is gentle — it should not be painful). Increase intensity gradually according to tolerance.

6

Uniwand technique (face)

Slowly and continuously glide the Uniwand along the treatment area — do not hold it in one spot. Recommended movements:

  • Around the eyes: circular or up–down motion under the eye.
  • Forehead: bottom-to-top or circular motions.
  • Around the mouth: along marionette lines from the mouth corner downwards.

The adjustable timer helps keep track of treatment time. DO NOT pass over the eye itself or directly over the eyeball.

7

Treatment frequency (manufacturer recommendations)

Manufacturer recommends facial treatment at least 5 times weekly for 8–12 weeks during the initial course. Then maintenance 2–3 times weekly. Body EMS is recommended 3–5 times weekly with 20–30 minute sessions — allow 48 hours recovery for the same muscle group.

8

Aftercare (skincare)

After treatment apply moisturiser, serum or a specialised anti-age cream on the face — microcurrent can make the skin more receptive to cosmetics. After body EMS rest or do light activity (walk). Do not train the same muscle immediately after EMS — allow recovery.

When NOT to use UniGlo?

UniGlo is a combined EMS + Microcurrent beauty device. Although stimulation is generally gentle, its use is contraindicated in certain conditions. If any of the following apply to you, do not start using it without consulting your treating physician.

  • Pregnancy — during the first 3 months do NOT use on the abdomen
  • Pregnancy — during the last 3–4 months do NOT use on the abdomen
  • Epilepsy or other seizure disorders (consult your physician)
  • Active or suspected cancer in the treatment area
  • Severe cardiovascular disease (uncontrolled hypertension, recent myocardial infarction, severe heart failure)
  • Acute skin inflammation, injury, fresh surgical scar or infection in the treatment area
  • Do NOT use the Uniwand directly around the eye (not over the eyeball or the white of the eye)
  • Avoid open wounds on the face (acne, herpes, dermatitis) when treating the face
  • Deep vein thrombosis or acute coagulation disorder in the treatment area
  • Carotid atherosclerosis — do NOT use on the neck
  • Skin sensory impairment (reduced sensation in the treatment area)
  • Children under 12 years (only under adult supervision and with physician approval)

UniGlo is a CE-marked medical device intended for home cosmetic use. Its use does not replace a medical or dermatological examination or professional cosmetic/aesthetic treatment. The device is intended as a COMPLEMENTARY tool used alongside a comprehensive skincare and lifestyle routine.

Realistic expectations: individual UniGlo results vary. It does not halt age-related skin changes and does not match the outcomes of professional cosmetic treatments. Meaningful change is expected after an 8–12 week initial course. If you do not see clear change, consider other cosmetic options.

New skin symptoms (rash, persistent redness, pain, itching, blisters): STOP USE IMMEDIATELY and consult a dermatologist. Allergic reaction to electrode pad adhesive is rare but possible.

UniGlo IS NOT a fat-burning device. Weight loss and lasting body shaping require active training and appropriate nutrition. EMS’s muscle-tone effects complement a comprehensive body-shaping routine.

Do not use the device while driving or performing operational tasks. Keep electrode pads clean and replace them in time.

Use only original TensCare accessories. Keep the device out of reach of children.

The information on this page is for general guidance and does not replace individual medical advice, diagnosis or treatment. For specific concerns always consult your treating physician.

It is particularly useful after prostate surgery: while electrostimulation-based rehabilitation gradually restores muscle strength, Prosecca gives day-to-day security. I write more about the complications of prostate surgery."

Realistic expectation
The effect is immediate but not permanent: the band works only while you wear it. Pelvic floor training or electrostimulation is needed to restore muscle strength – the two together are the most effective approach. Finding the optimal tension may take a few days of trial and error.
This is not the device for you if
you are looking for a permanent cure: the band is a symptomatic device and cannot restore muscle function. It is not sufficient on its own for severe, large-volume urine loss. It is not suitable for women.
Before you order
It is always worth having the cause of the dribbling examined by a urologist, especially if it persists months after surgery. Do not set the band too tight, and remove it immediately if you feel pain, numbness or see skin discolouration. Do not use it if there is skin damage or inflammation.

– Dr. Zsolt Zátrok
Physician, medical technology expert, blogger

Who do I recommend it for?

Urine dribbling is common after radical prostatectomy or TURP – rehabilitation can take weeks or months. The Prosecca band provides protection from the moment it is put on during rehabilitation: you do not need to worry while exercising, working, or performing daily activities. It is advisable to carry out electrostimulation therapy in parallel (e.g. PFE for Men) to restore muscle strength.

Prosecca can be worn discreetly while running, walking, cycling or training. Its lightweight, narrow design does not restrict movement while preventing dribbling.

If a few drops escape after urination – a common issue among men known as post-void dribble – the Prosecca band provides a discreet solution: you do not need to use a pad; the band prevents the dribble.

If you have been using incontinence pads, Prosecca is a durable alternative: you buy it once and reuse it many times. In the long run it is more economical than continually purchasing pads – and the mechanical protection is more targeted.

How does the compression band work?

The Prosecca band works on a mechanical principle: the padded surface applies a gentle, even pressure to the urethra and physically prevents urine passage. This is not therapy – it does not train the muscles and does not restore sphincter function.

When to use it? Use it during daily activities when you need protection: at work, during sports, or in social situations. Prosecca treats symptoms – it prevents dribbling.

What it is NOT for? Prosecca does not replace medical treatment or muscle training. The most effective approach: use the Prosecca band for daily protection alongside an electrostimulation device (e.g. PFE for Men or evoStim P) for pelvic floor muscle rehabilitation. As muscle strength improves, the need for Prosecca decreases.

How to use the Prosecca band?

1

Put the band on

Place the padded part on the underside of the penis along the urethra. The pad should be centred over the urethral line.

2

Tighten the Velcro

Tighten the band until the pressure is noticeable but not painful. The Velcro fastening allows fine adjustment of the pressure. With the correct tension, the dribbling will stop.

3

Wear it during daily activities

Prosecca can be worn while running, walking, sitting or exercising. Its narrow, lightweight design fits discreetly under underwear.

4

Remove before urinating

Open the Velcro before urinating and remove the band. Put it back on after urination. The Velcro enables quick on and off.

5

Cleaning

Wash daily with warm soapy water and dry. The smooth surface is easy to clean. Store in the supplied box.

Our medical expert says

“Paralysis or severe muscle weakness does not get better with rest — in fact, muscle can lose substantial strength and mass within days if it receives no stimulus. The OxyCycle 3 was built for this: its 80-watt motor will turn the pedal even if the patient cannot yet move actively, and as strength returns it can be switched gradually to active, resistance-based movement. It can be used for both arm and leg rehabilitation.”

Realistic expectations
The aim of passive movement is to maintain circulation, preserve joint range of motion and slow muscle wasting — not to trigger recovery by itself. Rehabilitation takes months, and outcomes depend on the extent of the injury. Daily regular use matters more than occasional long sessions.
This is not the device for you if
You are looking for a machine for high-performance training: the OxyCycle 3 is not designed for that. If the patient can already move independently and the main concern is knee or hip protection, a seated elliptical trainer gives a gentler movement path.
Before you order
The exercise program — duration, resistance, daily frequency — should be determined by the treating physician or physiotherapist, especially after stroke or surgery. DO NOT use the device without medical consultation in the presence of a fresh surgical wound on the affected limb, after orthopaedic or vascular surgery within the last four to six weeks, or when there is confirmed deep vein thrombosis or embolic risk.

– Dr. Zsolt Zátrok
Physician, medical technology expert, blogger

Who is the OxyCycle 3 intended for?

With partial or complete paralysis of one side (hemiparesis/hemiplegia) the affected arm and leg initially move little or not at all. In passive mode the motor takes over the movement, preventing joint stiffness and preserving basic muscle flexibility. As active movement gradually returns, resistance can be increased and switched to active pedaling. Continuous pedalling can also favourably influence limb circulation, supporting long-term recovery.

After hip or knee replacement, following extended hospital bed rest, or after any prolonged immobilisation, muscles quickly lose strength (up to 1–2% per day). Gentle, low-load pedalling can already be done while sitting in an armchair even when walking is still limited. Under the guidance of a physician or physiotherapist, the ergometer can be used as a supplementary mobilisation tool alongside the prescribed rehabilitation programme.

In chronic neurological conditions (MS, Parkinson’s, ALS, peripheral nerve injuries) the regularity and gentleness of movement therapy are especially important. The passive–active transition allows the patient to use the device according to their current condition: on worse days the motor assists, on better days they pedal more actively. A specialist (physiotherapist, neurologist) determines the recommended daily duration and intensity.

Many families face the problem of an elderly relative spending days in an armchair or bed because it’s difficult for them to go out. Motor-driven pedalling maintains blood circulation and joint range of motion even when walking is no longer feasible. The device operates quietly and can be used while watching TV — exactly the type of daily small activity that can help prevent chronic deconditioning.

Active and passive modes: how does the 80-watt motor work?

The principle of pedal rehabilitation ergometers is the combination of continuous, gentle joint mobilisation (continuous passive motion, CPM) with progressive loading as muscle strength returns. The difference between the two operating modes is as follows:

Passive mode: the motor drives the pedal

In this mode the 80-watt motor rotates the pedal axle at a steady cadence (between 25–65 RPM) — the patient’s leg or arm merely rests on the pedal and does not exert active force. Continuous passive motion can favourably influence joint range of motion, muscle length–tone relationships, and limb circulation. The CPM principle has been used for decades in post-surgical rehabilitation and neurological recovery.

↔️ Rotation in both directions (forward and backward)

In passive mode the OxyCycle 3 does not rotate in only one direction: the motor drives the pedal forward (clockwise) and backward (counterclockwise), and direction can be changed during operation. This is important because the two rotation directions produce different muscle activation patterns:

  • Forward rotation: during leg pedalling this emphasises the quadriceps (knee extensors) and hip flexors in the upward phase.
  • Backward rotation: places more emphasis on the hamstrings and gluteal muscles, and the joint movement pattern differs. The same applies to arm pedalling: the shoulder and elbow move through different ranges in the two directions.

Alternating direction within a session can support varied muscle-group mobilisation, which is often a clinical goal in rehabilitation practice.

Active mode: against adjustable resistance

In active mode the motor stops and the patient pedals using their own muscle strength. Mechanical resistance is continuously adjustable, so as muscle strength increases the training load can be measurably raised. This typically corresponds to the second–third phase of recovery when active movement has begun.

️ Built-in safety system (cramp-stop)

The device detects sudden increases in resistance in the limb (e.g., spastic cramp, muscle contraction) and automatically stops to avoid joint or muscle injury. This is especially important for post-stroke patients, where spasticity may occur at any time.

Frequently asked questions about the OxyCycle 3

Direction change is not fixed: it can be modified during operation with the switch. The device is intentionally designed this way because the two rotation directions activate different muscle groups and joint movement patterns:

  • Forward rotation: emphasises quadriceps and hip flexor work during leg pedalling.
  • Backward rotation: emphasises hamstrings and gluteal muscles.

The same applies to arm pedalling: the shoulder and elbow traverse different ranges in the two directions. Alternating direction within a session can support varied muscle-group mobilisation.

A 30 W motor may cope with a healthy, thin limb, but if the affected limb is spastic, cramping, or the patient is more severely deconditioned, the motor will “stall” as resistance increases. The 80 W provides substantially more reserve: a constant cadence can be maintained even if the limb’s passive resistance is high. This difference makes the OxyCycle 3 suitable for clinical use while remaining home-sized.

For severely bedridden patients, special bed-mounted rehabilitation devices are recommended — discuss these with the treating physician. With normal home use (30–60 minutes daily) the main mechanical components (chain, bearings, motor) are designed for several years of service. If it occurs often or is accompanied by severe pain, consult your treating physician or physiotherapist: the cadence may be too high or you may still need to use the device in passive mode.

How to use it at home? – Step by step

1

Positioning on a stable surface

Place the device on a smooth, level surface on the supplied anti-slip mat. For leg pedalling position it on the floor in front of the armchair/chair; for arm pedalling place it on a table at a comfortable reachable height. Sit comfortably with a straight back and knees slightly bent. The distance between the pedal and your knee should allow a full rotation without the knee fully extending to a stop or bending excessively beyond 90°.

2

Fitting the correct pedal

For leg pedalling use the full-foot pedals (non-slip surface). For arm pedalling switch to the hand pedals — the grip strap secures your palm to the pedal so it won’t slip off even with weak grip strength. The swap can be done by hand without tools.

3

Selecting the mode: passive or active

In passive mode the built-in motor rotates the pedal at the set cadence (between 25–65 revolutions per minute). The patient simply rests on the pedal, muscles are elongated, and joints are mobilised. In active mode the motor stops and the patient provides the propulsion against the set resistance. The two modes are switched with a control.

4

Setting cadence and direction

Cadence is continuously adjustable between 25 and 65 RPM. Start with a low value (25–30 RPM) — the goal is gentle, slow mobilisation, not athletic speed. In passive mode the rotation direction can be selected forward or backward, and can be changed during the session (see next section). Changing direction activates different muscle groups, so it’s worth alternating within a session.

5

Using the timer and LCD display

The 15-minute timer automatically stops the device after the set time elapses. The LCD display shows, either simultaneously or alternately: elapsed time, current cadence (RPM), total rotations, and estimated calories burned. These data are useful for the physiotherapist or treating physician to objectively follow progress.

6

Training rhythm: 1–2 hours daily, 30 min blocks

Manufacturer recommendation: maximum 1–2 hours daily, in 30-minute training blocks. Shorter 5–10 minute blocks are appropriate initially. The exact rhythm should always be determined by your treating physician or physiotherapist based on current condition and rehabilitation goals.

When NOT to use the device?

The pedal rehabilitation ergometer is strictly contraindicated without medical consultation in the following conditions:

  • Fresh surgical wound on the affected limb, or orthopaedic/vascular surgery within the last 4–6 weeks — do not use without the operating physician’s permission.
  • Acute, confirmed deep vein thrombosis (DVT) or embolic risk — moving the limb may be risky.
  • Acute joint inflammation, active arthritis flare, fever, or an infectious process in the affected limb or systemically.
  • Severe cardiovascular instability: untreated arrhythmia, unstable angina, recent myocardial infarction, uncontrolled high blood pressure — cardiologist approval required.
  • Fresh fracture or non-consolidated fracture of the limb in use, unstable joint prosthesis.
  • Severe osteoporosis — even gentle passive movement should be used only with medical advice.
  • Uncontrolled spasticity or severe contracture with very limited joint range — assessment by a movement therapist required.
  • Pregnancy — only with permission and guidance from the treating obstetrician.
  • Severe cognitive impairment where the patient cannot signal discomfort or pain — use only under supervision.
  • Children under 14 — only under the direction of a paediatrician or paediatric rehabilitation specialist.

Unsure? Always consult your treating physician or physiotherapist before use — the rehabilitation plan is individual and your condition should determine when and how to start.

Important information

The MoVeS OxyCycle 3 pedal trainer is a CE-marked device classified in the fitness/rehabilitation category, for home use. The information in this description is general and does not replace medical or physiotherapy advice. The exact rehabilitation programme (duration, cadence, mode, direction, resistance) should always be based on an individual assessment by your treating physician, neurologist, orthopaedic specialist, or physiotherapist.

Long-term improvement is achieved gradually, with regular use — do not expect immediate results and do not exceed the recommended daily duration. If any unusual symptoms occur (severe pain, swelling, skin discolouration, shortness of breath, chest complaints) stop training immediately and seek medical attention.

The product is marketed in accordance with the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR). The scientific references cited support the principle of active-passive ergometers; specific use always requires individual medical assessment.

Scientific references

The use of active-passive pedal ergometers in rehabilitation has decades of research backing. The following peer-reviewed publications analyse ergometer cycling in post-stroke and general rehabilitation:

  2. Stoller, O. et al. (2019). Ergometer Training in Stroke Rehabilitation: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis. Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation. (28 studies, 1115 stroke patients). PubMed
  3. Aydoğan Arslan, S. et al. (2019). Ergometer cycling improves the ambulatory function and cardiovascular fitness of stroke patients—a randomized controlled trial. Journal of Physical Therapy Science. PubMed
  4. Kaupp, C. et al. (2018). Rhythmic arm cycling training improves walking and neurophysiological integrity in chronic stroke: the AcceleRATE study. Journal of Neurophysiology. PubMed

What does photobiomodulation mean?

During soft laser treatment, tissues are exposed to light of a specific wavelength and dose. This process is called photobiomodulation (PBM).

How does the four‑channel PEMF system work?

The coils of the magnetic applicators create a time-varying magnetic field. The field can be applied through clothing, dressings and plaster.

Actual exposure is determined by field intensity, frequency, duty cycle, treatment time, number of coils, polarity, distance and placement together.

The manufacturer specifies an average of 200 Gauss per channel with a flexible applicator. The 800 Gauss figure is the device’s total capacity across four channels, not the field delivered to a single hip or spine.

The main advantage of the larger total capacity is operating multiple applicators simultaneously. It does not prove a specific centimetre-measured penetration depth or superior clinical outcome.

What can you use it for – details of the two functions

IontoBravo covers two different iontophoresis purposes in a single device: hyperhidrosis (tap water) and joint complaints (medicated). Each function requires its own preparation and protocol.

Tap water iontophoresis is a needle-free, drug-free solution for treating excessive palmar, plantar or axillary sweating. A mild electrical current is passed through the skin via tap water. Studies suggest this process temporarily influences sweat gland function.

Treatment protocol:

  • Initial phase (1–4 weeks): daily or every other day, 15–20 minutes/session.
  • Maintenance phase: 1–2 times weekly, 15–20 minutes/session.
  • PC (pulsed) mode: more comfortable, less irritating than DC.
  • Current: start from 5–10 mA, gradually to a comfortable level.

Effects are not immediate – improvement is usually felt after 2–4 weeks of regular treatment, with full effect by 6–8 weeks. Clinical studies report that the majority of patients (60–80%) experience significant reductions in palmar/plantar sweating.

In traditional iontophoresis, electrical current helps deliver anti-inflammatory agents (NSAIDs: diclofenac, ketoprofen) transdermally directly to the painful area. The advantage: the agent bypasses the digestive system, reducing gastric or hepatic load, and can reach higher concentrations in the target tissue.

Indications:

  • Joint inflammations (knee, shoulder, elbow, wrist)
  • Chronic tendinopathies (tennis elbow, Achilles tendon, patellar tendon)
  • Post-sports injury recovery
  • Peyronie’s disease (under urologist supervision)
  • Chronic osteoarthritis pain

Treatment protocol: Use DC (continuous) mode, set current per physician/physiotherapist recommendation. Treatment time 15–20 minutes. Frequency is set by the sports physician or rheumatologist according to complaint type.

DC (direct current): constant polarity current, effective for drug delivery. Recommended for traditional (medicated) iontophoresis. May be somewhat more irritating than PC in some cases.

PC (pulsed current): current acts in pulses. More comfortable and less irritating – recommended for tap water iontophoresis (hyperhidrosis). Research suggests similar effectiveness to DC for hyperhidrosis treatment, but better tolerability.

General recommendation: PC for hyperhidrosis, DC for medicated joint iontophoresis. However, your treating physician or physiotherapist may recommend differently for individual cases.

The mineral content of tap water varies by location. If your tap water is too soft (low conductivity), the current will not flow properly through the skin. Solutions:

  • Add 1 teaspoon of baking soda per tray – increases conductivity.
  • Use bottled mineral water – usually has sufficient mineral content.
  • DO NOT use softened or distilled water – it will not work!

If unsure, test: if you feel absolutely no tingling during treatment and the display current does not stabilize, the water conductivity is likely too low.

Both devices are CE-certified and suitable for tap water iontophoresis. The choice depends on individual needs:

IontoBravo advantages:

  • Dual function: tap water + medicated iontophoresis (joint treatment)
  • Both DC and PC modes
  • Usable by athletes for post-injury recovery

DermaDry advantages:

  • Automatic polarity switching (more convenient)
  • Purely hyperhidrosis-focused, simpler user interface

Choose IontoBravo if: you have joint complaints in addition to hyperhidrosis, or you are an athlete. Choose DermaDry if: your goal is only tap water iontophoresis and you want automated polarity switching.

Side effects of iontophoresis are typically mild and transient:

  • Mild skin redness, irritation – usually resolves quickly after treatment.
  • Tingling, mild stinging – normal, due to the current.
  • Temporary increased sweating – may occur after the first few treatments, then normalizes.
  • Skin dryness – use moisturizer after treatments.
  • Small blisters – with too high current; reduce intensity in such cases.

If side effects persist or worsen, stop treatment and consult your physician.

How to use it step by step?

1

Power preparation (AA batteries or mains adapter)

IontoBravo runs on 2 AA batteries or the supplied mains adapter. For long daily use the mains adapter is recommended; for occasional or mobile treatments battery operation is fine. Remove batteries if not used for a long time.

2

Choose function (tap water or medicated)

Decide what you want to treat: hyperhidrosis (tap water iontophoresis, PC mode) or joint complaint (medicated iontophoresis, DC mode). The two types require different preparation.

3

Tap water iontophoresis preparation (for hyperhidrosis)

Fill the treatment trays with lukewarm tap water (about 1–2 cm of water). Check there are no open wounds on the skin – you can cover minor injuries with petroleum jelly. If your tap water is too soft (low conductivity), add 1 teaspoon of baking soda or use bottled mineral water. DO NOT use softened or distilled water!

4

Medicated iontophoresis preparation (for joint complaints)

Apply the anti-inflammatory gel (on sports physician/physiotherapist recommendation, e.g. diclofenac or ketoprofen) to the painful area. Place the moist sponge cuff and the electrode over it. Polarity (negative or positive electrode) depends on the agent – the treating physician sets this.

5

Mode selection + intensity setting (0–25 mA)

For hyperhidrosis: PC (pulsed) mode, start at 5–10 mA, gradually increase to a comfortable level. For joint treatment: DC (continuous) mode, set current according to physician or physiotherapist recommendation. A mild tingling at the start is normal.

6

Perform treatment (15–20 minutes) + finish

Treatment duration is 15–20 minutes. For hyperhidrosis keep your hands/feet in the trays; for joint treatment the electrodes are fixed over the painful area. After treatment dry the skin and use a moisturizer. For tap water iontophoresis, initially daily or every other day, later 1–2 maintenance sessions weekly. For joint treatment follow medical protocol.

When NOT to use the IontoBravo?

The following situations may make iontophoresis dangerous or cause side effects. If any apply to you, do not start using the device without consulting your treating physician.

  • Wearing a pacemaker, implanted defibrillator (ICD) or any electronic implant
  • Metallic implant in or near the treated area (screw, plate, joint prosthesis)
  • Metal-containing intrauterine device (IUD)
  • Pregnancy or possibility of pregnancy
  • Arrhythmia or severe cardiovascular disease
  • Epilepsy or previous epileptic seizure
  • Open wound, acute infection or large-area skin injury at the treatment site
  • Polyneuropathy in the treated area (reduced or absent skin sensitivity – e.g. diabetic neuropathy)
  • Active malignant tumor near the treated area
  • Acute phlebitis or deep vein thrombosis in the treated limb
  • Skin irritation or eczema at the treatment site (avoid until healed)
  • Known allergy to the agent to be used (NSAID gel, e.g. diclofenac, ketoprofen)
  • Children for unsupervised use (under 12 years only with adult supervision)

Unsure? Consult your treating physician or dermatologist before use – especially with chronic diseases, medication use or any implanted medical device. For hyperhidrosis treatment consult a dermatologist; for joint treatment consult a sports physician or rheumatologist. What does photobiomodulation mean?

During soft laser treatment, tissues are exposed to light of a specific wavelength and dose. This process is called photobiomodulation, abbreviated PBM.

Light interacts with cellular light-absorbing molecules and can influence several biological processes. Research investigates its effects on cellular energy metabolism, local inflammatory signaling and regenerative processes.

The L2000 Pro uses four diodes of 500 mW each. The 20 Joule/10 seconds specification refers to the device’s total optical energy output, distributed over the larger treatment area. This is not equivalent to 20 J/cm² energy density.

The main advantage of the high total output is short treatment time. It does not mean you should always choose maximum power or longer sessions for every problem. Photobiomodulation is dose-dependent: more is not automatically better.

What does photobiomodulation mean?

During soft laser treatment tissues are exposed to light of specific wavelength and dose. This process is called photobiomodulation, or PBM for short.

Light interacts with the cells' light-absorbing molecules and can influence multiple interconnected biological processes. Research examines effects on cellular energy metabolism, local inflammatory signaling and regenerative processes.

The outcome is not determined by power alone. Wavelength, delivered energy, treatment area, treatment points and frequency are equally important. The L500 Pro's 500 mW output advantage is that it can deliver the selected energy dose in a short time.

Soft laser therapy is widely used in veterinary medicine. The 660 nm wavelength is suitable for superficial tissues in small animals – wounds, sutures, skin inflammations. Consult your veterinarian for a treatment protocol.

Tip: Trim hair from the treated area. Hold the laser 1 cm from the skin and treat each area for 30–60 seconds daily. Make sure the animal does not look into the laser beam!

What complaints can the SaltDome help with?

Salty air may help clear nasal passages and reduce mucosal swelling. Many allergy sufferers report milder symptoms when they start regular use 2–4 weeks before the season. Details: Hay fever and salt therapy.

How does inhaled salty air work?

The SaltDome nebulizes saline ultrasonically, releasing 2–5 micron salt particles into the air. This size, research suggests, can reach the lower airways — small enough to reach the bronchi yet large enough to deposit there.8 Salt that adheres to the mucosa can act in three ways:

  • Mucus thinning: salt’s osmotic effect draws water to the mucosal surface — like salting cucumber slices. Secretions thin and become easier to cough up and clear.8
  • Mucosal calming: salt particles may reduce mucus viscosity and help restore normal mucosal function, which can be beneficial in allergic conditions.1,8
  • Support for ciliary function: the tiny cilia that sweep mucus and debris outward can be reactivated; in chronic airway disease this function slows down, and salt therapy may aid its recovery.2

Central (brain/spinal cord) paralysis can also result from head trauma (car accidents, sports injuries), post-brain-tumour surgery phases, severe stages of multiple sclerosis (MS), or certain levels of spinal cord injury. The common feature is that the motor nerve to the muscle and the muscle itself are INTACT; only the brain command (motor neuron pathway) is damaged. DuoBravo N's ETS function targets this situation: remaining voluntary activity combined with stimulation assistance can help re-establish connections.
